collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A young villager realizes nobody knows why Isola's oldest joke is funny: ask an elder, or work out what the tall one was.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: There's a joke that's been told on Isola for generations. It goes: "Why did the fisher bring a ladder to the reef?" And the answer is: "Because of the tall one." Everyone laughs. Every single time. (friend), who has heard it all (friend.his/her) life, has just realized (friend.he/she) has absolutely no idea why it's funny.

choices.label: Try to Work Out What the Tall One Was

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) opens (subject.his/her) mouth to explain, stops, frowns, and thinks. "Because... the tall one... there was a tall one, and..." (subject.He/she) gives up. "I don't know either." They ask around. Nobody knows. Everyone laughs anyway. (friend) decides it's the greatest joke ever told, precisely because nobody understands it anymore. (friend.He/she) tells it at every fire for a month.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) is determined. The tall one was a fish? A wave? A person? (friend.He/she) asks (elder), the oldest villager, who laughs so hard at the question that no answer ever comes. Eventually (friend) decides the tall one is a lost piece of history and that's that. At the next fire, someone tells the joke, and (friend) laughs louder than anyone.
